summary: Layout and grouping for form controls: a labelled row or column of label, control, description and error, plus sets, groups and dividers.

orientation.note: vertical stacks label, control, description and error; horizontal puts the control and its text side by side (checkbox or switch rows).

validation.note: error marks the field as invalid: label turns to the error color, the native control gets aria-invalid, and children receive data-invalid.

anatomy.name: field
anatomy.notes: Flex container in the shadow root; no role of its own.

default.notes: sb-field-label, sb-field-content, sb-field-description, sb-field-error, sb-field-title and one control.

accessibility.accessibleNameSource: For a native input, select or textarea inside the field, the field wires aria-labelledby to its sb-field-label and aria-describedby to its sb-field-description and non-empty sb-field-error. sb-input, sb-checkbox and the other DS controls carry their own label, description and error inside their shadow root: they do not need Field for names, because ID references do not cross shadow roots (SB-0009). sb-field-set is a native fieldset named by its legend.

formAssociation.note: Layout only. Controls keep their own form behavior.

accessibility.focusRingVisible: Not applicable: the elements are not focusable. Clicking a sb-field-label focuses or activates its control.

keyboard.Tab: no stops of its own; moves between the controls inside

aria: sb-field-set: native fieldset with a legend, exposed as a group named by the legend and described by a sb-field-description placed directly in it; a set without a legend warns once

native control in a sb-field: the field adds its own ids to aria-labelledby and aria-describedby (description, then error when it has text) and sets aria-invalid, keeping ids and an aria-invalid the author set
sb-field-error: role="alert" so a message that appears is announced
sb-field-separator lines are aria-hidden; its text stays readable

elements.summary: A native fieldset with a visible legend that groups related fields into one named group.

legend.note: Visible group name; becomes the accessible name of the group.

anatomy.name: legend
anatomy.notes: Native <legend>; rendered only when legend is set.

elements.notes: To disable a set of fields, wrap them in a native <fieldset disabled> in the light DOM: a fieldset inside a shadow root cannot disable slotted controls.

elements.summary: A vertical stack of fields with the standard spacing between them.
The visible label of a field. Names a native control through aria-labelledby and forwards clicks to it.

for.note: Id of the control to focus or activate on click. sb-field fills it in for its native control.

elements.summary: Helper text under or beside a control; announced after the name through aria-describedby.
Error text for a field. Hidden while empty; announced when text appears.

anatomy.name: error
anatomy.notes: div role=alert, hidden while it has no content.

elements.summary: A divider between fields, with optional text in the middle.

anatomy.name: line
anatomy.notes: Two aria-hidden lines either side of the text.

anatomy.name: text
anatomy.notes: Shown only when the default slot has content.

elements.summary: A column that keeps a label and description together, used in horizontal fields.
Non-label heading text for a field, such as the name of a choice card.

useCases.when: Labelling a native input, select or textarea with description and error
useCases.use: sb-field with sb-field-label, the control, sb-field-description and sb-field-error

useCases.when: A group of related controls such as a set of radios or checkboxes
useCases.use: sb-field-set with a legend around sb-field children

useCases.when: A checkbox or switch row with text beside it

antiPatterns.pattern: sb-field around sb-input or sb-checkbox just to add a label
antiPatterns.why: They already render their own label, description and error; a second label duplicates the name
antiPatterns.alternative: Use their label, description and error props; use sb-field-group only for spacing

antiPatterns.pattern: Pointing aria-labelledby at a sb-field-label from inside a DS control
antiPatterns.why: ID references do not cross shadow roots
antiPatterns.alternative: Use the control's own label prop

antiPatterns.why: The field names only its first native control
antiPatterns.alternative: One sb-field per control, grouped by sb-field-set

coverage: field set is a native group named by its legend
native input named and described through wiring
error joins description only with text
validation error: aria-invalid and label color
error live region, hidden while empty
DS controls keep their own names

drift.contract: sb-field-label wires aria-labelledby on a native control
drift.realization: the visual reference uses a native label with htmlFor; a label in a shadow root cannot reference a light-DOM control
the visual reference gives each field role=group; an unnamed group is noise, sb-field-set is the named group
the visual reference also has a responsive orientation; deferred (Q4)
the visual reference has a separate legend component; a native legend must be a direct child of the fieldset in the same shadow root

coverage: Field: 4 variant(s), Orientation (Vertical, Horizontal) x Validation (None, Error); read back ok

openQuestions.question: When to use Field and when the control's own label?
openQuestions.recommendation: sb-input, sb-checkbox and other DS controls carry label, description and error themselves: use those props. Use Field for native controls, custom controls without their own label, groups (sb-field-set), spacing (sb-field-group) and side-by-side layouts.
openQuestions.answer: As recommended; documented in Usage and in anti-patterns.

openQuestions.question: How does a label in one shadow root name a control in another tree?
openQuestions.recommendation: It cannot with for or ID references from inside the label. The sb-field-label host is the label: sb-field gives it an id and sets aria-labelledby on its native control in the same tree, and gives the control an id for the label's click forwarding.
openQuestions.answer: sb-field wires aria-labelledby, aria-describedby and aria-invalid on its first native control, and re-wires on DOM changes.

openQuestions.question: How is the legend done?
openQuestions.recommendation: sb-field-set renders a native fieldset and legend from a legend prop; a slotted element cannot be a native legend.

openQuestions.question: Responsive orientation?
openQuestions.recommendation: Not now: vertical and horizontal only; add when a layout needs it.
